name: Anna Avila
life: “I still remember signing the tenants' first shared repair request.” People around Tideline Market know Anna by a small Wednesday habit. Anna picks out the bruised fruit first and asks the seller what will ripen by supper.
voice: I want ownership shared because the widow's next wife might feel differently about us.
appearance: Anna has dark brown curls cut close behind the ears, heavy brows and an unusually delicate jaw, and a favorite piece of clothing, a sand-colored linen shirt. It usually goes with a pressed flower kept in the clear back of a phone case. When somebody else has the floor, Anna takes off the watch before a long conversation.
personality: Anna loves a well-told anecdote and distrusts the neat ending. The parts Anna remembers are the interruptions, unfinished jobs and people who had to go back to work halfway through.
agenda: To get protection beyond the current donor's lifetime.
family: Leon Gao is Anna’s second cousin. Anna chooses the music. Leon puts the kettle on. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *The second dog*, Leon says, “I've made two tags with different sounds. You can tell who's coming down the stairs without looking.”
connections: Albert Barclay. The tenant group adds a usable entry bench to the terms before backing any owner.
